properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 — the classic SHA-family implementation used by Ethereum tooling — is declared in the trading bot's package-lock.json; the build ships SHA-1/SHA-2 hashing capability transitively.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is declared on both sides of this object: crypto-js@4.2.0 (implements SHA-1 among its hash functions) in the Solana bot's package-lock.json, and the sha1 crate in the PumpFun Rust Cargo.lock. The collision-broken hash ships with both builds.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: crypto-js@4.2.0 is declared in the Solana trading bot's lockfile (transitive; not imported by first-party TS source). crypto-js ships MD5 among its primitives, so MD5 is available in the shipped build; no call site found in the application code. Changeable here by removing/upgrading the dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Solana trading bot's lockfile declares the secp256k1 stack: secp256k1@4.0.3, @noble/secp256k1@1.7.1 and @types/secp256k1 — ECDSA-secp256k1 capability (the Ethereum curve) ships in the build via the bot's EVM-side dependencies. Quantum-unsafe signature curve.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey@1.0.x (an implementation of OpenSSL's EVP_BytesToKey single-round MD5 KDF) is declared in the trading bot's lockfile both directly and under ganache — weak-by-practice password-to-key derivation ships in the dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt-pbkdf is a transitive dependency of the Ethereum dev tooling (truffle/ganache, a devDependency of the trading bot); it is a bcrypt-based KDF. The app itself is a Solana bot that does no password hashing — the package is shipped with the devDependency tree only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Math.random() (predictable PRNG) generates the Yellowstone gRPC subscription's SESSION_HASH in both entry points of the trading bot. It is a session identifier passed with the subscription request — real weak randomness in a session-ID context, though its role is stream labeling/deduplication rather than authentication, which limits practical impact to identifier guessability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: k256 (RustCrypto secp256k1) is a transitive dependency in the latency-comparison crate's Cargo.lock; the crate's own source only streams gRPC/websocket data. ECDSA/secp256k1 is Shor-vulnerable; availability in the shipped dependency tree is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is declared in the bot's lockfile via the ethers/web3 dependency chain; its secp256k1 module provides ECDSA signing and ECDH. No first-party call site — availability in the build is the fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ed25519 is the Ed25519 implementation behind @solana/web3.js Keypair (tweetnacl-adjacent stack). It is genuinely exercised: the bot constructs Keypair.fromSecretKey() wallets that sign transactions (see the source-level Ed25519 finding at index.ts:18-21). Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; changeable here only via Solana protocol, realistically fixed upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 capability ships on both sides of this shard: @noble/curves@1.9.7 in the TypeScript bot's package-lock.json and the Ed25519 crates in the Meteora Rust Cargo.lock — declared dependencies; the build ships Ed25519 (quantum-unsafe signature scheme) whether or not the app calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh (Node's ECDH binding, backed by elliptic) is a transitive dependency of ganache — the local Ethereum dev chain pulled in by the truffle devDependency. ECDH key agreement is shipped with the dev tooling; the Solana bot itself performs no ECDH. Availability is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key-agreement capability ships via tweetnacl@1.0.3 in the TS bot's lockfile and the X25519/curve25519 crates in Meteora's Cargo.lock — quantum-unsafe key agreement available in the built artifacts. Related to ALG-82f1eeb2 (Curve25519) and LIB-f69df116 (curve25519-dalek), which describe the same Rust dependency from different angles.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the classical JS ECDSA library, a transitive dependency (via ganache/truffle dev tooling) in the bot's tree. Same logical asset as LIB-a0bfbc1a (elliptic@6.5.4) — marked same_as there.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek@3.2.1 is declared in the Meteora DLMM instruction-streamer's Cargo.lock — Curve25519 scalar math (X25519/Ed25519 building blocks) ships in the built Rust binary via the Solana SDK crates.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.9.7 declares P-256 among its curve implementations in the trading bot's package-lock.json — NIST P-256 (ECDSA/ECDH) capability ships in the build via the bot's EVM-side dependencies. Quantum-unsafe curve, same library entry also carries the Ed25519 object's npm site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's SHA-3 variant) enters via ethers ^6.2.3, a direct dependency of the trading bot. Hash family is quantum-safe (Grover halves preimage security only); this is dependency-inventory coverage, no remediation urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 enters the tree via ethers (@ethersproject/pbkdf2, wallet HD derivation) and the truffle/ganache dev tooling, plus the pbkdf2 Rust crate in the Meteora lockfile (via its TLS/dependency chain). Iteration counts are not visible at declaration sites; the npm pbkdf2 module defaults to sha1+ iterations chosen by callers. Dependency-inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js enters via ethers (wallet key derivation) and truffle/ganache dev tooling. Two major versions (2.0.4 and 3.0.x) are shipped in different dependency sub-trees. No first-party call site; dependency-inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 ships via @noble/hashes@1.8.0 in the TS bot's lockfile and the sha2 crate in Meteora's Cargo.lock — the standard hash of both ecosystems, declared as a dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 is available on both sides of the polyglot tree: via @noble/hashes in the bot's npm tree and via the blake3 crate in Meteora's Rust lockfile. Quantum-safe hash (Grover only); low-urgency inventory coverage.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The hmac@0.8.1 crate is declared in the Meteora Cargo.lock — HMAC (keyed MAC) ships in the built binary, pulled in by the Solana/web3 crate stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 provides AES (its default usage is CBC mode with EvpKDF); the mode is not visible at the declaration site. Same package also carries the MD5 object (ALG-70109388) — both are availability facts for the shipped build, no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes' SHA-3 (standard FIPS 202, not Ethereum's keccak256) — distinct implementation and package from the keccak/@ethersproject entries under ALG-052c24b2, so both objects stand separately. Quantum-safe; low urgency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring@0.17.14 is declared in the Meteora Cargo.lock — the ring provider (AES-GCM AEAD plus classical TLS key-exchange primitives) ships in the build. ring 0.17 offers no post-quantum KEX, so anything negotiating through ring uses classical groups only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@1.0.3 (XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox — a strong AEAD) is declared in the Solana bot's package-lock.json, pulled in by Solana/web3 tooling; authenticated encryption ships in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is the Ed25519 + XSalsa20-Poly1305 library behind @solana/web3.js — it is the actual implementation the bot's Keypair.fromSecretKey()/sign chain reaches. Genuinely exercised at runtime by every wallet instantiation in Bots/Typescript/Solana-trading-bot.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 ships MD5, AES, SHA, HMAC, PBKDF2, RC4-drop etc. It is a transitive dependency (no first-party import found in the TS sources). The MD5 and AES algorithm objects (ALG-70109388, ALG-0eb2c0da) are the algorithm-level views of this same package; this object is the package-level record.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring is the crypto provider actually installed for rustls in first-party code: general-grpc-examples/Rust/yellowstone-accounts-watcher/src/main.rs:16 calls rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider().install_process_level() (verified), and ring is also declared in Meteora's Cargo.lock. The "." group-marker site is the summary of that source-level use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is declared not only in the Bots lockfile but in ~10 further TS example lockfiles (PumpFun/Typescript, Raydium/Typescript projects) — the "." group-marker site summarizes those. Provides sha2/sha3/blake2/blake3/hkdf/pbkdf2/scrypt primitives behind the Solana web3 stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls is the TLS library behind every Rust gRPC example in this repo (tonic ClientTlsConfig), declared in the Cargo.toml of rabbitstream-timestamp-monitor and yellowstone-accounts-watcher (the "." group-marker site) and in Meteora's Cargo.lock; live provider install verified at yellowstone-accounts-watcher/src/main.rs:16-18. Released rustls negotiates classical X25519 ECDHE by default — no ML-KEM hybrid group support in the pinned/available versions; migration rides on upstream rustls.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is declared in the Bots lockfile and ~10 further TS example lockfiles; it provides the secp256k1/P-256/ed25519 curve implementations behind the web3 stack. Algorithm-level view of the same package: ALG-92b28f71 (secp256k1). Availability in the shipped builds is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: One logical asset as the PBKDF2 carrier in a polyglot tree: npm pbkdf2@3.1.2 in the Bots lockfile and the pbkdf2 Rust crate in Meteora's Cargo.lock. Algorithm-level view: ALG-4de3b020 (marked same_as here).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The openssl@0.10.80 Rust crate (bindings to the system OpenSSL) is declared in the Meteora Cargo.lock — the built binary links the platform's libcrypto; the runtime OpenSSL version decides TLS and PQ capability, which this tree does not pin. Observable here, decided by the runtime platform.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: native-tls@0.2.18 is declared in the multi-stream-checker's Cargo.lock — that tool's TLS sessions run over the platform's OpenSSL stack (SChannel on Windows), with PQ capability decided by the runtime platform's OpenSSL version rather than anything in this tree. Observable here, replaceable only at the platform level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls@0.21.12 is declared in the Meteora Cargo.lock — the build ships a TLS 1.3 stack, but rustls 0.21 (ring-backed, pre-aws-lc) supports classical key-exchange groups only (X25519 etc.); gRPC TLS sessions from this binary cannot negotiate a hybrid post-quantum group at this version. Upgrading rustls to 0.23.x with the aws-lc-rs provider is the migration path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Package-level record of the same logical asset as ALG-6e1f67ab (ECDSA secp256k1 via k256): the k256 crate is the secp256k1 ECDSA implementation declared in the latency-comparison crate's lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Package-level record of the scrypt-js carrier (the 2.0.4 copy under @truffle/interface-adapter plus the 3.x copies) — same logical asset as ALG-c1f8b585.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
